claims.text: A machine-learning-assisted free-energy approach can accurately predict the melting properties of high-melting refractory materials.
Potentials trained on limited DFT data can replace full ab initio molecular-dynamics thermodynamic integration for these calculations.
The ML-assisted approach requires only a fraction of the computational cost of full ab initio molecular-dynamics thermodynamic integration.
The proposed calculation concerns a refractory material in its high-temperature solid phase near its melting point.
The ML interatomic potential is trained on selected DFT configurations.
Representative high-temperature DFT training and validation data are required for the ML model.
The ML interatomic potential reproduces the DFT energy landscape governing interatomic interactions.
The ML potential captures the essential physics of interatomic forces and phase behavior.
Capturing interatomic forces and phase behavior enables efficient and reliable free-energy calculations.
The free-energy calculations can determine melting temperature, entropy of fusion, enthalpy of fusion, and volume change at melting.
ML-assisted predictions will agree well with results from traditional ab initio molecular-dynamics calculations.
The ML-assisted method will reduce computational expense sufficiently to make high-throughput screening viable.
The approach is expected to be applicable to refractory materials with well-behaved DFT energy landscapes.
Complex electronic correlations may limit the effectiveness of the ML-assisted approach.
Insufficient DFT training data may limit the effectiveness of the ML-assisted approach.
Transferability and accuracy may vary across different refractory materials and complex melting behaviors.
